sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Supervision only works if the memo reaches the right desk, fast.

Daily situation reports arrive every morning. Reading each by hand, matching every case to a station and typing each memo from scratch took days — while the lapse went cold. The generator reads the report, resolves the responsible officer and drafts the memo within minutes of upload.

The problem

Drafting took days

Each report was read by hand, every case matched to a station, and each memo typed from scratch.

Now · drafts ready within minutes of upload

Who was responsible?

Stations, sectors and transfers change. Working out which officer held that ground on that date was slow and error-prone.

Now · resolved from jurisdiction and personnel records

Repeat lapses went unseen

Nobody could easily see that the same officer had already been warned twice this cycle, so repeat lapses never escalated.

Now · three warnings raise a charge memo

Every case walks down the hierarchy to one desk

A city force is organised zone → division → circle → police station → sector. The generator resolves each case through that chain and picks the officers who held that ground, using officer records synced from the personnel system so transfers are respected.

RecipientRoleMemo
Station house officerHolds the stationSHO memo
Primary sector officerHolds the sectorSector memo
Relief sector officerCovers leave and duty gapsIf on duty
Circle supervisorSupervisionVisibility only

Memo lifecycle and escalation

Every memo has a status

  1. DraftGenerated from the case, editable before anything is issued.
  2. Pending reviewIn the reviewing authority's queue.
  3. ApprovedIssued to the officer.
  4. Awaiting replyThe officer must respond.
  5. CompliedReply uploaded and closed.

A memo can also be held for more facts, or rejected if the lapse is not upheld — in which case it does not count towards escalation.

Three warnings, then a charge memo

  • Only approved warnings count. A warning counts once the reviewing authority approves it. Held or rejected memos do not.
  • The fourth lapse becomes a charge memo. After three approved warnings, the generator offers a charge memo instead of another warning.
  • The count resets each cycle. Once a charge memo is raised, the warning count starts again.

Each role sees only what it needs

Administrator

Runs the report intake, checks extracted cases and categories, and keeps officer access and organisational hierarchy right.

Reviewing authority

Sees the review queue and the force-wide picture: approve, hold or reject each memo, edit wording before approval, and see lapses by station and category.

Officers

See only memos addressed to them: read the memo and the case, upload a compliance reply, and track their own warning count.

Safeguards

  • A person approves every memo — the generator drafts; only the reviewing authority issues, and wording can be changed before approval.
  • Every memo traces to a case — tied to the situation report entry it came from.
  • Officer data respects transfers — synced from personnel records, so the memo reaches whoever actually held that ground.
